The wiring diagram image was not provided. Connections follow the text: the matrix is powered from the Nano Matter 3V3 pin and controlled over I2C (SDA, SCL), plus GND. The Grove matrix is 3.3 V compatible, so 3V3 is correct.

The Nano Matter sits on the breadboard, as in the photo. The exact breadboard columns are assumed, because the board's pin order was not available. Only the four pins used (3V3, GND, SDA, SCL) are shown in holes 3t.e, 4t.e, 6t.e and 7t.e. Each jumper wire goes into row a of the same column strip. The other Nano pins are not used.

The Grove cable in the photo is modelled as four jumper wires (red 3V3, black GND, white SDA, yellow SCL) going from the breadboard to the matrix's Grove pins. The cable's wire colours were guessed from the photo.
The USB-C cable goes from the Nano Matter to a computer for power and programming. The computer is not modelled.
The Eero Thread Border Router, Amazon Alexa and the smart speaker are network and software items, not circuit parts, so they are not modelled.
The sketch also drives the Nano Matter's onboard RGB LED and button. They are built into the board and need no external parts.
